input: The recommendation is a metered trial on one of the three refrigeration lines before any capital decision. The plant engineer owns the trial. A food plant uses 2198 MWh of electricity per year in refrigeration. A heat-recovery retrofit is projected by the equipment vendor to save 12% of that use, a derived saving of 264 MWh per year at the vendor figure. Capital cost is $415k. At an electricity price of $0.09 per kWh, the derived annual saving is $24k and the derived simple payback is 17.3 years. The trade-off is $415k of capital against a derived $24k per year: a payback of 17.3 years at the vendor figure. The saving figure is a vendor projection and was not measured at this plant. Refrigeration load in the summer peak month was not modelled, so the annual figures rest on the vendor's projection spread over a year whose peak month is unexamined. The trial exists to replace the projection with a measurement on one line under the plant's own operating pattern. Metering one line bounds the cost of finding out: the retrofit is neither approved on a projection nor rejected without evidence, and the capital decision waits for the trial result. If the measured saving on the trialled line falls short of the projection, the derived payback lengthens beyond the stated figure and the case for the remaining lines weakens with it. At its stated scope, the position is a trial first, owned by the plant engineer, with the capital decision held until measured savings replace the vendor figure.
